payload.markdown: Namespaces have cleaned up much that was ugly about object-oriented PHP. We no longer have to tolerate ridiculously long class names or risk naming collisions (legacy code aside). On the other hand, with aliasing and with relative namespace references, it can be a chore to resolve some class paths so that they are fully qualified.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Namespaces: Named scopes that prevent class-name collisions and organise code.
References: Two variables sharing one value slot, created with =&.
Scope: Where a variable is visible: global, local, static and closure scope.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Null Safe Operator: ?-> short-circuits an entire chain when the receiver is null.
Object Identity: === compares instance identity: two objects with equal fields are still distinct.
